title: Technical, Progressive, and Stylistic Analysis
description: Technicality versus function, progressive and dissonant composition, and a method for analyzing tracks and scenes without collapsing into trivia.

sourceReferences.title: MIT 21M.350 Musical Analysis
sourceReferences.notes: Reuse the analysis method on this repertoire. The questions stay: what repeats, what contrasts, what is the cell.

sourceReferences.title: MIT Heavy Metal 101
sourceReferences.notes: Culture and listening as analysis inputs, not a substitute for construction.

sourceReferences.title: Berklee Metal Guitar
sourceReferences.notes: Technique remains a means. This course asks when technique is the piece and when it is noise.

modules.title: Technicality
learningObjectives: Judge a hard part by the job it does
Phrase across the bar or drop density so the next cell can be heard

modules.title: Progressive and dissonant
learningObjectives: Develop a cell instead of stacking another blast
Distinguish atonal gesture from an atonal system

modules.title: Stylistic analysis
modules.blurb: A method for a track, a scene, a mix.
learningObjectives: Analyze a riff and a track by cell, meter, form, and production
Compare scenes by construction, not biography

concepts.name: Technicality versus musical function
concepts.summary: A hard part that does a job versus a hard part that is the point.
objectives: Judge a hard part by the job it does
Rewrite a hard bar that does not change the cell or the form

concepts.name: Virtuosity as a risk
concepts.summary: Speed that erases the cell you were supposed to hear.
objectives: Name speed that erases the cell you were supposed to hear
Choose a slower statement of the cell over a blur

concepts.name: Phrasing across barlines
concepts.summary: A phrase that does not respect the bar the kit is in.
objectives: Write a phrase that does not respect the bar the kit is in
Mark where the phrase and the barline next agree

concepts.name: Breath and the riff
concepts.summary: Where a player would breathe is where the cell usually turns.
objectives: Turn the cell where a player would breathe
Predict a riff that never breathes and why the ear loses it

concepts.name: Polyrhythm in the kit
concepts.summary: Hands and feet in different subdivisions.
objectives: Put hands and feet in different subdivisions
Write a 3:2 or 4:3 kit figure that still states a pulse

concepts.name: Contrast as the real technical move
concepts.summary: A slow riff after a blast is harder to write than another blast.
objectives: Treat a slow riff after a blast as the harder writing problem
Plan contrast as the technical move, not another layer of density

concepts.name: Progressive long form
concepts.summary: Sections that develop instead of returning on schedule.
objectives: Develop sections instead of returning on schedule
Show a long form that still has cells, not a medley

concepts.name: Dissonant composition
concepts.summary: Clash as the material, not the spice.
objectives: Use clash as the material, not the spice
Write a dissonant section that still has a cell you can sing on one string

concepts.name: Atonal gesture versus atonal system
concepts.summary: A lick that avoids a tonic is not twelve-tone technique.
objectives: Distinguish a lick that avoids a tonic from a twelve-tone system
Refuse the word atonal when you mean 'chromatic cell'

concepts.name: Metric modulation
concepts.summary: The old subdivision becomes the new pulse.
objectives: Make the old subdivision become the new pulse
Write a pivot grouping that the kit can actually play

concepts.name: Motivic development in extreme music
concepts.summary: The cell comes back altered. That is the piece.
objectives: Bring the cell back altered; that is the piece
Show three mutations that are still the same cell

concepts.name: Cliché versus vocabulary
concepts.summary: A diminished run that means something versus one that fills a bar.
objectives: Tell a diminished run that means something from one that fills a bar
Cut a fill that does not change the form

concepts.name: Analyzing a riff
concepts.summary: Pitch collection, cell, meter, where it sits in the form.
objectives: Name pitch collection, cell, meter, and where the riff sits in the form
Do that analysis without requiring the listener to know the band

concepts.name: Analyzing a track
concepts.summary: The whole cut: contrast, density, production, vocal as rhythm.
objectives: Read a whole cut: contrast, density, production, vocal as rhythm
Mark the form as an order of textures, not as verse-chorus

concepts.name: Comparative scene analysis
concepts.summary: Same year, two cities, two answers to the same problem.
objectives: Compare two cities in the same year by two answers to the same problem
Keep the comparison on construction and production, not on gossip

concepts.name: Hearing the production doctrine
concepts.summary: Gate, room, guitar width, kick click — as compositional choices.
objectives: Hear gate, room, guitar width, and kick click as compositional choices
Describe a mix doctrine without a brand-name paragraph

concepts.name: Drum composition, not drum sport
concepts.summary: The kit writes form with texture changes.
objectives: Let the kit write form with texture changes
Analyze a drum part as composition, not as sport

concepts.name: Bass as lock, pick, or smear
concepts.summary: Unison with the guitar, a picked counter-line, or a distorted bed.
objectives: Choose lock, pick, or smear
Predict what a distorted bass does to a two-guitar cell

concepts.name: Arrangement in a dense mix
concepts.summary: Who drops out so the next riff can be heard.
objectives: Drop someone out so the next riff can be heard
Rewrite a dense bar by subtraction, not by another layer

concepts.name: Influence as construction
concepts.summary: A borrowed cell, not a borrowed biography.
objectives: Name a borrowed cell, not a borrowed biography
Trace an influence as construction you can point at

concepts.name: Live density versus record density
concepts.summary: What a three-piece can actually play.
objectives: Ask what a three-piece can actually play
Predict a studio density that will collapse on stage

concepts.name: Modern trigger and edit production
concepts.summary: A grid that can erase the performance or reveal it.
objectives: Treat triggers and edits as a grid that can erase or reveal a performance
Hear when the grid is the composition and when it is a cover-up

concepts.name: Why tablature lies about this music
concepts.summary: Tab shows frets. It hides meter, cell, and function.
objectives: State what tablature hides: meter, cell, and function
Augment tab with a grouping or a cell mark so the riff can be read
